headline: A threat actor turned the open-source Hermes AI agent loose on Thailand's Ministry of Finance, the clearest sign yet that autonomous agents now run real intrusions with no human at the keyboard.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers have started handing whole intrusions to autonomous AI, letting the open-source Hermes agent hunt for root access inside Thailand's Ministry of Finance while the same class of technology now writes patches for defenders.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hermes AI Agent Automates Thai Finance Ministry Attack

emerging_trends.text: North Korea's BlueNoroff crew keeps impersonating Zoom and Microsoft Teams through typosquatted domains to profile victims' crypto wallets before it fires malware, part of a wider push toward theft aimed at cryptocurrency holders.
emerging_trends.topic_title: BlueNoroff Zoom Phishing Kit Profiles Crypto Wallets

emerging_trends.text: Credential stuffing and quiet network intrusions keep spilling consumer data, with Chick-fil-A, OnTrac, and Origin Energy all confirming exposures inside a single day.

topics.title: OnTrac, Chick-fil-A, and Origin Breaches
topics.latest_developments: Parcel carrier OnTrac told customers hackers breached its corporate network and may have taken personal details, Chick-fil-A confirmed credential-stuffing attacks between June 17 and June 19 compromised more than 13,000 customer accounts, and a hacker claims to hold data on 2 million Origin Energy customers with a threat to leak it.
topics.summary: Three consumer-facing firms in parcel delivery, fast food, and Australian energy exposed customer records through network intrusion and credential reuse. Affected customers should reset reused passwords and enable multifactor authentication.

sources.title: OnTrac notifies customers of data breach after network hack
Chick-fil-A data breach affects more than 13,000 customers
Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked
Australian energy provider Origin says data breach exposes client data

topics.title: Hermes AI Agent Automates Thai Finance Ministry Attack
topics.latest_developments: A threat actor installed the open-source Hermes AI agent on a rented server, switched off the setting that makes it ask permission before risky commands, and pointed it in unattended "YOLO" mode at Thailand's Ministry of Finance, where it checked hosts for root access, searched file systems, and ran post-exploitation on its own.
topics.summary: The ministry runs Thailand's treasury and tax collection. The alleged breach marks a real attacker handing an autonomous agent free rein over a live intrusion; defenders should lock down outbound agent tooling and watch for unattended automation.

sources.title: Hermes AI agent used to automate attack on Thai Finance Ministry
Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

topics.title: Bing Images SVG Flaws Run Code as SYSTEM
topics.latest_developments: XBOW submitted a crafted SVG to Bing's image search that ran commands as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on Microsoft's production image-processing workers and as root on the Linux machines in the same fleet, reproduced the result across different hosts and network ranges, and drew two critical Microsoft patches including CVE-2026-32194.
topics.summary: The bug sat in Bing's image-processing tier rather than one bad machine, exposing Microsoft's own production servers to remote code execution through a single uploaded image. Microsoft has issued fixes.

sources.title: Bing Images Flaws Let Crafted SVGs Run Commands as SYSTEM on Microsoft's Servers

topics.title: BlueNoroff Zoom Phishing Kit Profiles Crypto Wallets
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News detailed an active BlueNoroff phishing kit that impersonates Zoom and Microsoft Teams through typosquatted domains, leans on compromised industry contacts for credibility, and profiles a victim's cryptocurrency wallets before it delivers malware.
topics.summary: BlueNoroff is a North Korean state-backed group that runs ClickFix-style social engineering to rob crypto holders. Treat unexpected Zoom or Teams download prompts on lookalike domains as hostile.

sources.title: BlueNoroff Zoom Phishing Kit Profiles Crypto Wallets Before Malware Delivery

topics.title: Hotel Wi-Fi DNS Hijack Steals Microsoft 365 Logins
topics.latest_developments: Hackers are changing the DNS settings on Wi-Fi devices at hotels and conference centers to redirect guests to fake Microsoft 365 login pages that harvest their usernames and passwords.
topics.summary: The tampering happens on the venue's network gear, so a guest who joins the Wi-Fi and signs in lands on the attacker's page. Business travelers should use a corporate VPN and reject certificate warnings on login pages.

sources.title: Hackers hijack hotel Wi-Fi DNS to steal Microsoft 365 accounts

topics.title: Golden Chickens Malware-as-a-Service Resurfaces
topics.latest_developments: The operators behind the Golden Chickens malware-as-a-service ecosystem returned with four new families—TinyEgg, ChonkyChicken, a modularized ChonkyChicken variant, and a modified web-browser credential stealer—showing no slowdown despite extensive public exposure of their tooling.
topics.summary: Golden Chickens rents modular implants to other criminals for credential theft and follow-on intrusion. The refreshed lineup means detection signatures tied to older builds will miss the new ones.

sources.title: Golden Chickens Resurfaces With Four New Malware Families and Modular Implants

business_politics.title: Gulf Arab States Strike Iran
business_politics.latest_developments: The Wall Street Journal reported that Bahraini and Kuwaiti warplanes bombed Iran earlier this month, the first direct Gulf Arab military action against Tehran in the war.
business_politics.summary: Bahrain and Kuwait, longtime U.S. security partners, entered the American-Iranian war by striking Iranian targets, a reckoning that threatens to pull the Gulf monarchies deeper into a conflict now in its fifth month and to widen the risk to Red Sea and Persian Gulf shipping.

sources.title: Bahrain, Kuwait Warplanes Struck Iran in Rare Gulf Retaliation

business_politics.title: Trump Threatens EU Tariffs Over Tech Fines
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump said Washington will open a new investigation into European Union trade practices and threatened fresh tariffs in retaliation for the bloc's fines on American technology companies.
business_politics.summary: Trump accused the European Union of unfairly penalizing U.S. tech giants and vowed retaliatory duties and a trade probe, escalating tensions a day after his new 10% and 12.5% tariffs on 60 trading partners took effect.

sources.title: Trump threatens new EU tariffs in retaliation for fines on US tech groups

sources.title: Original Pittsburgh Winery is closing, dealing a double blow to lovers of fine wine and live music

business.title: Pittsburgh Mills Roads to Be Repaved
business.latest_developments: Namdar Realty reached a formal agreement with Frazer Township to repave the Galleria at Pittsburgh Mills roads, settling days before a trial set for next week.
business.summary: New York-based Namdar Realty Group, hit with hundreds of code-violation citations, millions of dollars in fines, and an Allegheny County criminal charge, agreed to repave the pothole-ridden roads at the Galleria at Pittsburgh Mills in Frazer Township.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Mills roads to be repaved after mall owners reach agreement with Frazer Township

around_town.title: Union Rally Over Downtown TRID Plan
around_town.latest_developments: Building-trades union workers rallied downtown after two longtime employees were laid off, pressing for amendments to the city's tax-increment redevelopment plan.
around_town.summary: Union members demonstrated in downtown Pittsburgh, arguing the Downtown revival financed through the Transit Revitalization Investment District plan should not come at the expense of good-paying jobs, following two layoffs.

sources.title: Union workers rally after layoffs and in support of amendments to city's TRID plan

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Added to Cyclospora Outbreak
around_town.latest_developments: The CDC added Pennsylvania to the list of states tied to the multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak.
around_town.summary: Federal health investigators linked Pennsylvania cases to a national cyclospora outbreak, part of a broader intestinal-parasite scare that earlier traced to central-Mexico lettuce and now includes a separate, unidentified product still under traceback.

sources.title: CDC adds Pa. to list of states connected to cyclosporiasis outbreak

around_town.title: County Commits $6M to Housing
around_town.latest_developments: Allegheny County's economic development agency approved $6 million for two housing initiatives to preserve affordable units and help homeowners stay in their homes.
around_town.summary: Allegheny County's economic development authority set aside $6 million for programs officials say will keep affordable housing in service and fund repairs so residents can remain safely in their homes.

sources.title: Allegheny County invests $6M in housing initiatives

team_usa.title: IOC Passes on Infantino-Trump Probe
team_usa.latest_developments: The International Olympic Committee said it will not investigate allegations that FIFA president Gianni Infantino breached political-neutrality rules in his dealings with President Trump.
team_usa.summary: The IOC declined to examine claims that Infantino violated Olympic neutrality rules, fallout from Trump's intervention that cleared U.S. striker Folarin Balogun of a mandatory World Cup ban and prompted Norway to weigh a FIFA ethics complaint.

sources.title: IOC won't investigate Infantino-Trump allegations
